questions.q: In Azure ML, what is a component?
options: A pipeline step with defined inputs, outputs, and a command and environment to run it
questions.explain: A component is one step with a well-defined interface (inputs and outputs) plus the command, code and environment that run it.

questions.q: In the Python SDK, how do you connect a training step to a preceding data-prep step?
options: Give both steps the same name
Set both to the same compute
Pass the prep step's outputs (for example prep.outputs.train_data) as inputs to the training step
questions.explain: Using one step's outputs as another step's inputs is what builds the dependency graph.

questions.q: What does the default is_deterministic: true on a component allow?
options: Azure ML may reuse the previous result when the inputs have not changed
The step always runs on a GPU
questions.explain: When inputs are unchanged, a deterministic component's earlier result can be reused instead of re-running it. Set it to false to force a re-run.

questions.q: Why register a component in the workspace?
options: It is required before any job can run
So it gets a name and version that teammates and other pipelines can reuse
questions.explain: Registered components are versioned and shareable, so pipelines can reference them (for example azureml:my_train@latest) without copying code.

questions.q: In the local demo, what connected the prep script to the training script?
options: Only output folders and command-line flags
questions.explain: The scripts shared nothing except the folders and arguments passed on the command line, which is exactly the component contract.
